tasks.title: Essay: Language and Belonging
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write an essay summarising and evaluating the key points from both texts in 240–280 words. Use your own words throughout as far as possible, and include your own ideas in your answers.

promptBlocks.label: Text 1
promptBlocks.text: For migrants, learning the dominant language of a new country is often presented as the single most important step towards integration. Without it, access to employment, housing and public services is severely limited, and the risk of social isolation increases dramatically. Yet the pressure to abandon one's first language in favour of the new one can create a painful sense of loss. Many migrants report feeling that they are expected to erase part of their identity in order to belong. A responsible approach to language learning would acknowledge this tension, offering support that values linguistic diversity rather than demanding assimilation. The goal should be functional bilingualism, not replacement. This argument also matters because institutions shape the choices available to individuals and communities over time, influencing responsibility, trust, and practical judgment.

promptBlocks.label: Text 2
promptBlocks.text: The idea that migrants can maintain their heritage language while fully integrating into a new society is well-meaning but unrealistic. In practice, limited time and resources mean that most newcomers must prioritise the language of their adopted country if they are to secure stable work and participate in civic life. Heritage language maintenance, while emotionally valuable, often comes at the cost of slower progress in the majority language, which can have long-term economic consequences for both individuals and their children. A responsible language policy must therefore be honest about trade-offs: it should encourage rapid acquisition of the host language while providing optional, not compulsory, support for heritage languages. This argument also matters because institutions shape the choices available to individuals and communities over time, influencing responsibility, trust, and practical judgment.

tasks.title: Review: Language Support Programme
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: A specialist magazine for language educators is running a series of reviews of community-based language support programmes for adult migrants. You decide to write a review of a programme you have observed or participated in. In your review, describe the programme and its approach to language learning, assess how effectively it balances the practical goal of rapid language acquisition with the emotional and cultural needs of learners, and recommend whether other communities should adopt a similar model.

tasks.title: Report: Language Provision for Newcomers
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: You are a consultant hired by a regional integration agency. The programme coordinator has asked you to write a report on how current language learning provision affects the sense of belonging among adult migrants in the region. In your report, analyse the main strengths and weaknesses of existing language courses in fostering both linguistic competence and social inclusion, assess the potential consequences for community cohesion if these weaknesses are not addressed, and propose two concrete actions the agency could take to improve the balance between practical language training and cultural affirmation.

tasks.title: Article: Language and Identity
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: An English-language online magazine for international readers is publishing a series on 'Language and Belonging'. You have been contacted by the editor, who asks you to write an article explaining your position on whether migrants should be expected to prioritise learning the host country's language over maintaining their mother tongue. In your article, discuss what you see as the main tension between integration and identity preservation, describe one practical consequence of your preferred approach for language policy, and suggest how communities could support both goals simultaneously. End your article by requesting that the magazine arrange a follow-up discussion with readers and language educators to explore the issue further.
